title: Playing carnival balls with Al Streeman
summary: Coquille played many carnival balls with Streeman; other bands got shares too; he describes the ball's colour and the carnival organizations.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Yeah, anything that old can hold up. I was going to ask you about carnival balls. That's one thing we never talk much about. You mentioned playing on the truck.

Right, I did my share of carnival balls during the Alstream in 19 years. We had our share of the carnival balls. You know, I played my share of them. I did, you know, the tableau and the supper dance and the whole works. Mm-hmm. For many years, yeah. Al had his portion of it, you know. There was bands like Russ Papalia, Rene Louap, and in the old days, let's see. Johnny Detroit. Bands of that caliber and bands like that, they used to all get a certain percentage of the balls. So I feel like I did my share of them.
Never having seen one in my whole life.
You haven't seen a carnival ball?
I've never had one in to go, particularly.
Well, if you've seen one, actually, you've seen them all. Let's put it that way. Like you see one parade, you've probably seen all the parades and Mardi Gras for it. That goes.
Well, it's always impressed me that sitting there in a tuxedo and watching other people's dance is not 100%.

Well, the ladies enjoy it, I think, more than the men. It's a very colorful affair. You see, in New Orleans, you have about 65 carnival organizations here, which all the big prominent businessmen belong to. And of these 65 carnival organizations, there might be about 20 big rich carnival organizations out there at 65, and they'll each give a parade. And after the parade, then a parade goes down to the municipal auditorium, and they have the carnival ball, and they have the tableau, which always depicts some theme of the past. And then there's 12 dances or 12 call-outs, and the girls that are called out or the young ladies that are called out. It's a very formal affair. Everything is formal. The girls in the evening gowns, the ladies in the evening gowns, the men in their tails and tuxedos. And the 12 call-outs, the young ladies don't know who it is that's calling them out. And while they dance in the gentleman that belongs to the organization who is still masked, he gives the young lady a souvenir or what we call a favor. It might be a little vanity or something like that, you know. And then after the 12 call-outs, there's usually public dancing amongst everybody for about a half hour. And the ball might end at 12 o'clock or it might end at 1 o'clock in the morning. And then from 1 to 3 or from 12 to 3, there might be a supper dance at one of the hotels. By the same organization, they go to the supper dance and usually have to cost $15 or $20 to attend the supper dance because they put on a big feed. And there's a band there playing for the supper dance. So it's an all-day and all-night affair. Not all-night, not all-day, but I mean it's an all-night and all-morning affair for those who attend the supper dance. It's a very colorful affair and the women really enjoy it.
